messages.subject: Re: Error in survey report
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the error says: " camOp may only contain positive values (set scaleEffort = FALSE in cameraOperation()."
Did you try creating the camera operation matrix with scaleEffort = FALSE, i.e.:

camop_problem  <- cameraOperation(..., scaleEffort= FALSE)

I can't think of any other reason why there would be negative values in the camera operation matrix.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jurgen,

First, thank you for your reply and apologies for not answering your post before.
I actually managed to workaround that problem, but I didn't understand why in spatialDetectionHistory() I would need to set byCamera=FALSE in cameraOperation. The idea of setting byCamera=TRUE was to be able to check whenever one of the cameras in the pair would fail, which would affect detection parameters, because I am inputing effort in my secr models. So, if one station (two cameras) is entirely operational, the effort is 1, if one of the cameras of the station is off, effort is 0.5, and if none are operational, then effort is 0. This coding (0, 0.5, 1) as input for the secr modelling, in the trap file with header 'usage'.

Thanks again for your attention.
Henrique

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Install Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
that is some Mac issue and most likely not related to camtrapR. See here  <https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/6511>and here <https://community.rstudio.com/t/ide-package-update-fails/20164/2>. The links also provide potential solutions. Using install.packages() should be easier than using the tgz file.
When installing from a tarball the dependencies ( ‘generics’, ‘sf’, ‘sp’, ‘secr’, ‘data.table’, ‘lubridate) are not installed automatically, hence the installation of camtrapR fails. So you'd need to install them first, and this can be a pain to do manually.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error in surveyReport
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
this error means that there are stations in your record table that are not found in your camera trap table.

Try with the GitHub version, it gives a better error message than the CRAN version. See this commit <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/commit/cdc23935664bb1ed7f32bed5eae99f0a59820265>. To install:

install.packages("R.rsp")
remotes::install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: Errors using "spatialDetectionHistory" function
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
in cameraOperation(),
byCamera = T means that each camera is treated as an individual "station". In most scenarios that doesn't make much sense since multiple cameras at a station are usually near each other.

byCamera = F means that both cameras are combined into a single "station". This is normally the preferred choice. It also allows accounting for incomplete effort at individual cameras. If camerasIndependent = TRUE (cameras facing different directions), then effort per (full) day can be 2, 1, or 0 (depending on whether both, one, or no camera was active). If camerasIndependent = FALSE (paired cameras observing the same spot), then corresponding effort would be 1,1, or 0 (with two, one, and no camera active).

The problem is that spatialDetectionHistory expects a camera trap table with one row per station though, not two (for the coordinates at each station). So one can't just use the same camera trap table as for cameraOperation and instead aggregate by station first. Not ideal, I'll try to find a solution for that.

See below for a worked example. Two stations, one with two cameras and the other with one camera, and some cameras malfunctioning. The example works with byCamera = FALSE and accounts for incomplete effort.

data("camtraps")

# simulate camera trap table with two cameras at "StationA" and one camera at "StationB"
camtraps$Station <- c("StationA", "StationA", "StationB")
camtraps$camera <- c("cam1", "cam2", "cam3")
camtraps$Problem1_from[2] <- "01/05/2009"   # StationA/cam2 malfunctioned for a few days
camtraps$Problem1_to[2] <- "10/05/2009"

camop_problem <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps,
                                 stationCol   = "Station",
                                 cameraCol    = "camera",
                                 byCamera     = F,
                                 allCamsOn    = F,
                                 camerasIndependent = T,
                                 setupCol     = "Setup_date",
                                 retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
                                 writecsv     = FALSE,
                                 hasProblems  = T,
                                 dateFormat   = "dmy"
)

camtrapR:::camopPlot(camop_problem)

data(recordTableIndividualSample)
recordTableIndividualSample <- recordTableIndividualSample[recordTableIndividualSample$Station != "StationC",]

# aggregate camera trap table with multiple entries per station to one row per station
# only relevant for coordinates, which are averaged (= midpoint between cameras)
camtraps_by_station <- aggregate(camtraps[, c("utm_y", "utm_x")], by = list(camtraps$Station), FUN = mean)
colnames(camtraps_by_station)[1] <- "Station"

sdh <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableIndividualSample,
                               species               = "LeopardCat",
                               camOp                 = camop_problem,
                               CTtable               = camtraps_by_station,   # instead of camtraps
                               output                = "binary",
                               stationCol            = "Station",
                               speciesCol            = "Species",
                               Xcol                  = "utm_x",
                               Ycol                  = "utm_y",
                               individualCol         = "Individual",
                               recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                               recordDateTimeFormat  = "ymd HMS",
                               occasionLength        = 10,
                               day1                  = "survey",
                               includeEffort         = TRUE,
                               timeZone              = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"
)

# warning is because camtraps was modified to make up this example

# effort is incomplete due to malfunction. Takes both cameras into account (independently)
usage(traps(sdh))
           o1 o2 o3 o4 o5
StationA 18.0 20 19 11  7
StationB  7.5 10 10 10  0

zip package: as you said, it was probably already installed since you got a zip file already.
plots on top of plots. I've never seen this before and have no idea what is going on. Does this happen with any call to plot(), or only with the camtrapR functions?

Best regards

messages.body_plain:
Yes, possibly an R or RStudio issue, maybe specific to Mac. I don't know what causes it. Updating RStudio and R is always worth a try.

You may be able to prevent this issue by calling dev.off() between plots. It closes the current plot and resets the graphics device.

Another workaround in this scenario is to call the camtrapR plot functions with writePNG= TRUE. The saved plots should not have any overplotting. If you find a proper answer or a solution please let us know.
Best regards
